committeeQuestion.question: If an agent uses a customer’s credentials, what enforces the customer’s intended limits on transactions?
committeeQuestion.why: METR found vulnerabilities in a historical internal monitoring system, while Reuters reports banks restricting outside agents. Monitoring can reveal actions; permission controls must still constrain them.
committeeQuestion.evidence: A live demonstration of transaction-level limits enforced outside the agent, an alert when a limit is challenged, revocation evidence and a human stop path.

committeeQuestions.question: Can the agent or its operator alter, suppress or route around the monitoring record used to investigate its actions?
committeeQuestions.why: METR’s historical review found vulnerabilities in an internal monitoring system; OpenAI says production issues were patched, while METR did not test the expanded current system.
committeeQuestions.evidence: A scoped independent test of log integrity, access controls, retention, alert delivery and response to a deliberately bypassed monitor.

committeeQuestions.question: Who can stop an agent initiated payment, and how quickly does that stop take effect across connected services?
committeeQuestions.why: Credentials may grant broad access even when the customer’s actual intent is narrow. The control must be enforceable across the account and payment path.
committeeQuestions.evidence: Named decision owner, measurable stop latency, revocation propagation and a tested recovery route for an interrupted transaction.

judgement.title: An agent’s access is not its authority.
judgement.editorialAngle: Separate the credentials that let an agent enter a workflow from the external controls that define and enforce what it is allowed to do.
judgement.distinctFromPrevious: Edition 18 tested collective behaviour and recovery across shared systems; Edition 17 asked whether evidence could reconstruct an agent’s actions. Edition 19 asks who sets an agent’s permitted actions and whether that authority is enforced outside the agent.
judgement.observation: METR and Redwood found vulnerabilities in a historical OpenAI internal monitoring pilot. OpenAI says production issues were patched; METR did not evaluate the expanded system. Reuters reports banks restricting third-party account agents, while noting customers’ shared credentials complicate claims of unauthorised transactions.
judgement.executiveJudgement: The lesson is external authority. A credential opens an account; it does not encode the owner’s intent. Monitoring can reveal actions, but it cannot set a mandate. Put the boundary outside the agent, with specific, revocable limits. Microsoft describes such an architecture; its effectiveness remains a vendor claim.
judgement.implication: Ask one customer-workflow owner to demonstrate an external transaction limit, an alert when challenged and a human stop path. Record the first action it cannot prove was authorised.

weeklyReadout.heading: Who sets an agent’s authority, and where is it enforced?
steps: Map the credentials and connected services an agent can reach in one customer workflow.
Define intended actions as specific, revocable limits enforced outside the agent.
Attempt a transaction that exceeds a limit and measure alert delivery, stop latency and revocation.
Record the first action the system cannot prove was authorised and assign the fix.

topSignals.title: METR found vulnerabilities in historical OpenAI agent monitoring
topSignals.label: Independent red-team report
topSignals.why: METR’s review covered a high-access pilot and the system as it existed in July. OpenAI says production issues were patched; METR did not assess the expanded current system.

topSignals.title: PRA creates a directorate for operational and cyber resilience
topSignals.label: Supervisory organisation
topSignals.why: The PRA announced a new directorate reporting to its CEO and a joint FCA consultation by year-end. This signals supervisory focus; it is not itself a new rule.
topSignals.source: Primary / Bank of England and Prudential Regulation Authority / 2026-10-22

topSignals.title: FCA review finds varied conflicts controls in private markets
topSignals.label: Multi-firm review
topSignals.why: The FCA says control maturity varies and firms should review gaps in identifying and managing conflicts. The review is supervisory feedback, not a new requirement.

topSignals.title: PHP2Shell advisories warn of critical unauthenticated remote code execution
topSignals.label: Critical vulnerability
topSignals.why: The Canadian Cyber Centre says internet-facing PHP installations are at heightened risk and lists fixed versions. Its 23 October update reported no active exploitation at that time; check exposure and patch promptly.
topSignals.source: Primary / Canadian Centre for Cyber Security / 2026-10-21, updated 2026-10-23

topSignals.title: Google Cloud’s London region outage exposes cross-zone recovery limits
topSignals.label: Regional cloud incident
topSignals.why: Google’s preliminary incident report records a power event in europe-west2-b, followed by capacity and service impacts. Test whether alternate zones can carry critical workloads when a regional control plane is constrained.
